subject: Recap: mapping projected volumes to monthly spend & procurement thresholds
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Elliot James <elliot.james@finware.io>, Sofia Morales <sofia.morales@finware.io>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: mapping projected volumes to monthly spend & procurement thresholds

Hi Elliot / Sofia —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a proposed next step so procurement has what they need. Main takeaways from our side: 

- Target start: mid-Jan pilot (weeks to provision dedicated capacity if needed).
- Two usage scenarios you gave on the call:
  1) Conservative: 5M tokens / month (mainly search + short chat prompts)
  2) Growth: 50M tokens / month (chat-heavy & reranking spikes)
- Budget band you mentioned: $7k–$45k / month (needs to fit existing PO thresholds).
- Procurement constraint: standard PO limit at FinWare is $25k/month without VP approval — above that requires SOW + legal review (you flagged).

What I’m attaching: rough mapping that converts tokens -> expected $/1M (based on the model families we discussed) and three procurement-friendly options:

A) Start small (Conservative): hosted API, monthly pay-as-you-go, ~ $7k/mo for ~5M tokens.
B) Stepped commit: 12-month tiered commit that locks 25–30% discount around 30M tokens/month (keeps spend under $25k for initial quarters).
C) Dedicated reserve: reserved capacity for 50M+ with committed monthly invoice (requires PO + security checklist).

Ask / next steps: can procurement confirm whether a rolling 3-month PO that maxes at $25k/mo would work as the initial path? If not, we should plan for an SOW and legal intake. Also, Elliot / Sofia — please confirm the expected token mix (prompt vs. completion avg tokens) so we can tighten the $/1M estimate.

I’ve attached a simple workbook (FinWare_Q3_usage_estimates.xlsx) showing line items for $/1M at different model classes + estimated monthly spend under each scenario.

Happy to hop on a 20-min alignment call with procurement and finance if that helps.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Sales Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: FinWare_Q3_usage_estimates.xlsx, Redwood_provisioning_options_summary.pdf
From: Elliot James <elliot.james@finware.io>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Morales <sofia.morales@finware.io>, procurement@finware.io
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 16:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: mapping projected volumes to monthly spend & procurement thresholds

Lauren —

Thanks for the concise recap and the workbook — that helped. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Token mix: for the pilot we expect a high read ratio — ~80% embeddings/search/rerank (short queries, ~40 tokens total) and ~20% chat completions (average completion ~220 tokens).
- The $7k baseline aligns with our conservative estimate given the chosen open model family.
- Procurement note: our finance team will not approve anything above $25k/month without VP sign-off. VP signoff is possible, but the review clock is ~3–4 weeks and typically needs a procurement-ready PO + attached SOW.

We’d like to aim for the stepped commit path (Option B), but initial quarter needs to stay under the $25k/month ceiling. If Redwood can provide a 3-month trial/discount bridge or a short-term credit to flatten the ramp, that would make the internal approval much easier.

Also cc’ing procurement — can you confirm whether a 3-month rolling PO (max $25k/mo) + a 6-month review is acceptable from your side?

Cheers,
Elliot
Elliot James
Head of Product
FinWare
elliot.james@finware.io
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Elliot James <elliot.james@finware.io>
Cc: Sofia Morales <sofia.morales@finware.io>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, procurement@finware.io
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: mapping projected volumes to monthly spend & procurement thresholds

Elliot / Sofia / Procurement —

Appreciate the clarity. Quick responses inline: 

- Token mix: thanks — we’ll re-run the workbook with 80/20 split and attach an updated total $/mo estimate by EOD.
- Short-term bridge: Redwood can offer a one-time onboarding credit equivalent to ~20% of the first-month committed spend or a 3-month step-down credit (we usually structure as credits in month 1–3 to ease procurement signoff). We can put that in writing in the commercial email so procurement has a number to approve.
- PO construct: a rolling 3-month PO capped at $25k/month with a 6-month review is workable from our commercial side. If you plan to execute a longer-term commit in Q2, we’ll prepare a sample SOW and the typical SLA appendix to include in legal review.

Attached: updated workbook with the 80/20 mix and a short PDF that maps the three procurement-friendly paths to expected monthly invoices.

Next steps I suggest: 
1) Procurement confirms whether we should prepare a 3-month rolling PO (we’ll send sample PO language and a PO template).
2) Redwood sends a commercial summary email for formal approval (including the onboarding credit and price band).
3) If procurement needs the SOW to start legal intake now, we can loop in legal and provide a draft.

If helpful, I can schedule a 20-min call tomorrow with our finance ops (Neha) to answer specific billing/invoice questions.

– Lauren

Quick note from finance ops: 

- We reviewed the updated workbook — with the 80/20 split the estimate for the conservative scenario (5M tokens) lands at ~$6.8k/month (hosted). Growth scenario peaks at ~$42k/month if they hit the 50M tokens at the higher-latency model family.
- Onboarding credit option (3-month step-down) is approved: we can structure credits to reduce the first three invoices by 10% / 7% / 3% respectively, and we will include that in the commercial summary.
- PO template: attaching a redlined PO template and a short checklist of required security artifacts for the procurement team (see PO_template_FinWare.pdf).

I’m available for the 20-min call Lauren suggested — propose Thu 11/12 at 10:00am PT.

-Neha

Attachments: PO_template_FinWare.pdf
